gopro.name: GoPro
gopro.description: Blurry and sharp pairs made by averaging consecutive frames of 240 fps GoPro videos of dynamic scenes, with camera and object motion. The sharp target is the middle frame of the averaged window.
gopro.blur_source: Synthetic: average of 7 to 13 consecutive 240 fps frames (about 29 to 54 ms)
gopro.timing: 240 fps capture; the spacing of the blurry frames is not stated
gopro.used_here: Test split: 11 sequences, 1,111 pairs, the plain blur input (the averaging without the gamma 2.2 curve of blur_gamma)
gopro.splits: Train 22 sequences, 2,103 pairs; test 11 sequences, 1,111 pairs

reds_val.name: REDS
reds_val.authors_short: Nah, Baik, Hong, Moon, Son, Timofte, Lee
reds_val.description: Clips recorded at 120 fps, interpolated to a virtual 1920 fps by a frame-interpolation network and averaged into 24 fps blurry video through a calibrated camera response, then downscaled to 1280×720.
reds_val.blur_source: Synthetic: interpolated to 1920 fps, averaged with duty cycle 0.8 at 24 fps (about 33 ms) in signal space
reds_val.capture: GoPro HERO6 Black, 1920×1080 at 120 fps, 300 clips
reds_val.used_here: Validation split: 30 clips × 100 frames = 3,000 pairs, val_blur (no compression); the test ground truth is not released
reds_val.splits: Train 240 clips, validation 30, test 30, 100 frames each

bsd2.name: BSD 2ms/16ms
bsd2.description: Real video recorded by two synchronized cameras behind a beam splitter: one takes a 16 ms blurry exposure through a neutral-density filter, the other a 2 ms sharp exposure centered inside it.
bsd2.blur_source: Real capture with a beam-splitter rig, no synthetic averaging
bsd2.capture: Two cameras of the same model (not named), ND filter cutting the blurry camera's light to 1/8
bsd2.timing: 15 fps; 16 ms blurry, 2 ms sharp exposure (BSD also has 1 ms/8 ms and 3 ms/24 ms settings)
bsd2.used_here: Test split of the 2ms/16ms setting: 20 sequences × 150 frames = 3,000 pairs
bsd2.splits: Per setting: train 60 × 100 frames, validation 20 × 100, test 20 × 150
bsd2.licence: Not stated (the repository code is MIT)

dvd.name: DVD
dvd.authors_short: Su, Delbracio, Wang, Sapiro, Heidrich, Wang
dvd.description: Hand-held 240 fps videos from several phones and cameras. Each 30 fps blurry frame averages a window of 7 frames with optical-flow interpolation between them; blur is mostly camera shake.
dvd.blur_source: Synthetic: 7 frames at 240 fps (about 29 ms) with 10 interpolated images per gap, centered on the sharp frame
dvd.capture: Hand-held phones and cameras at 240 fps (iPhone 6s, GoPro Hero 4 Black, Canon 7D for training; other devices for testing)
dvd.timing: 30 fps output, every 8th frame kept as the sharp target
dvd.resolution: Mostly 1280×720 JPEG; one test video is 720×1280
dvd.used_here: The 10 quantitative test videos × 100 frames = 1,000 pairs, every frame (the paper scored 30 frames per video)
dvd.licence: Not stated (the repository code is MIT)

realblur_j.name: RealBlur-J
realblur_j.description: Real blurred and sharp photos taken at the same moment by two cameras behind a beam splitter, in dim indoor and night scenes with hand-held camera shake. RealBlur-J uses the cameras' JPEG output.
realblur_j.blur_source: Real capture: 1/2 s blurred and 1/80 s sharp shots of static scenes, hand-held shake
realblur_j.capture: Two Sony A7R III with Samyang 14 mm lenses behind a beam splitter
realblur_j.timing: Still images; 1/2 s and 1/80 s shutters opening together
realblur_j.resolution: About 670×760 (camera JPEG downsampled by 4 and aligned; sizes vary by a few pixels)
realblur_j.used_here: Test split: 980 pairs from 50 scenes, PSNR and SSIM by the official ECC-aligned evaluation
realblur_j.splits: Train 3,758 pairs from 182 scenes; test 980 pairs from 50 scenes

realblur_r.name: RealBlur-R
realblur_r.description: The same shots as RealBlur-J, made from the camera raw files with white balance and demosaicing only, so without the camera's tone curve; the sharp images are also denoised with BM3D. The images are therefore much darker.
realblur_r.blur_source: Real capture: 1/2 s blurred and 1/80 s sharp shots of static scenes, hand-held shake
realblur_r.capture: Two Sony A7R III with Samyang 14 mm lenses behind a beam splitter, raw files
realblur_r.timing: Still images; 1/2 s and 1/80 s shutters opening together
realblur_r.used_here: Test split: 980 pairs from 50 scenes, PSNR and SSIM by the official ECC-aligned evaluation
realblur_r.splits: Train 3,758 pairs from 182 scenes; test 980 pairs from 50 scenes
